page: Microsoft Azure L160iaos_v5 is an isolated, storage-optimized server within the Laosv5 series powered by dedicated AMD x86_64 processors. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers 160 dedicated vCPUs and 1,040 GB of system memory, which provides 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Its isolated physical allocation ensures full access to underlying host execution units without resource contention from co-located virtual machines.

The primary differentiator of the L160iaos_v5 is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which delivers 138,240 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity alongside Premium Storage compatibility for remote managed disks. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, directing all platform capacity toward core compute, memory throughput, and high-speed disk operations. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned with the instance.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of 160 vCPUs, more than a terabyte of memory, and massive local NVMe disk volume establishes a dense platform for I/O-heavy enterprise operations. Workloads that match this profile include massive distributed databases such as Cassandra or MongoDB, large data warehousing clusters, transaction-heavy SQL deployments, and intensive extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L160iaos_v5 is a dedicated, storage-optimized instance within the Laosv5 family built on x86_64 AMD processors. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the isolated virtual machine is provisioned with 160 dedicated vCPUs and 1,040 GB of RAM, providing an allocation of 6.5 GB per vCPU. The instance is highlighted by an extensive local storage footprint comprising 138,240 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, enabling high-throughput data persistence directly on the physical host. It contains no GPU hardware and supports Premium Storage capabilities for external disk configurations. The architecture is engineered for enterprise-scale workloads characterized by high I/O demands, such as massive distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, data warehousing, and transactional systems requiring low-latency local storage and substantial multi-core processing power without multi-tenant resource sharing.
